concepts.title: Resources: Human and Non-Human
concepts.definition: A resource is anything usable to satisfy a need. Resources divide into human -- time, energy, knowledge, skills -- and non-human -- money, goods, community facilities and natural materials; each again may be individual or shared. Values and habits decide whether these are used or squandered.
concepts.key_idea: Time, energy, money and skills are all one currency -- resources -- and management is spending them wisely.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe104.txt resource sections (concept of a resource, human and non human, individual and shared resources, values and resources)
question_patterns: define a resource and classify resources with examples
in class 11 management of resources: distinguish human resources from non human resources
give examples of individual and community resources
why are time and energy called human resources
how do values influence the use of resources
list the resources a student commands

solution_steps.explain: Call a thing a resource only if it can be used to meet a need or reach a goal.
Time, energy, abilities sit in people; money, goods, facilities sit outside -- both must be managed.
Some resources are personal, some shared by family or community -- use rules differ accordingly.

concepts.title: Management Process: Planning, Organising, Implementing, Controlling
concepts.definition: Management is the decision process that turns resources into goals: planning what to do, organising means and tasks, implementing the plan, and controlling by judging results against the standard. The loop feeds back -- judged outcomes revise the next plan.
concepts.key_idea: Plan, organise, act, check -- the four-beat rhythm that converts resources into achieved goals.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe104.txt management sections (management process, planning, organising, implementing, controlling, evaluation and feedback)
question_patterns: describe the steps of the management process
in class 11 management of resources: why is planning called the first step
what does controlling mean in resource management
apply the management process to organising a birthday at home
how does feedback improve the next plan

solution_steps.explain: Fix the goal, list tasks, allocate resources and time to each task.
Arrange materials, people and sequence, then carry out the work as scheduled.
Compare results with the standard, find the gap, and feed corrections into the next cycle.

concepts.title: Time and Energy Management; Work Simplification
concepts.definition: Time and energy are the human resources that technique can stretch: schedules and to-do lists discipline time, while work simplification -- better sequence, fewer motions, right tools, combining tasks -- saves energy. Rest and posture conserve the worker as much as the work.
concepts.key_idea: Schedule the hours, simplify the motions -- stretch the two resources that cannot be bought.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe104.txt technique sections (time management tools, energy management, work simplification, sequence of work, posture and rest)
question_patterns: how can a student manage time better
in class 11 management of resources: explain work simplification with examples
what techniques conserve energy in household work
prepare a daily schedule for exam week
how does proper posture save energy
distinguish time management from energy management

solution_steps.explain: List tasks, rank by importance, and slot them into a written schedule with buffers.
Rearrange sequence, gather tools beforehand, combine steps -- each cut motion saves energy.
Correct posture, seated work where possible, and short rests keep energy available till the task ends.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Apply the four steps of management to organising a study plan before exams.

solution_template.explain: Goal: syllabus covered. List subjects, weigh difficulty, allot hours per day.
Gather notes and papers, fix the daily timetable, and follow it.
Each evening check chapters done against plan; adjust next day's slots to close the gap.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A homemaker cooks, launders and supervises homework every evening and feels exhausted. Suggest work-simplification measures.

solution_template.explain: Soak and start the laundry before cooking so machines work while she cooks.
Keep ingredients and tools laid out before starting -- fewer trips, fewer motions.
A seated task between standing ones, with a fixed short rest, restores energy for homework supervision.
